touches.text: Proofs run against a TESTING database, separate from live.

A proof MAY read the live database; what a test writes stays out of live, either in the TESTING database or marked as a testing artifact that the rest of the system ignores. WHY: reading live saves populating test data; ignoring testing artifacts keeps them from leaking into what the system believes. Test against live, marked as testing. -amm
It launches each device's cairn/devices/<device>/groundloop/pulse.py, each as its own process (5.8.3.4).
pulse.py is part of the shim. The ground loop calling it tells the shim the pulse has arrived, and starts the shim if it isn't running.
Any shim, through its pulse.py, brings the bus up if it's down: whatever is called brings up what it needs (5.3.4.1).
Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.

A seal is host independent: one record per proof, whichever box asks. Seals are made by one sealing machine in the cairn device, and there is only ever one cairn (until a laptop dies and a backup takes over), so there is one sealer. A box that is not cairn's home asks the sealer instead of writing its own seal.

The seal is checked where the proof runs, not in the command's text: a proof refuses to run outside the tester's seal, so no spelling reaches the live ~/.cairn. proofgate only rewrites the common spelling for convenience. CC's decision, Q#101.
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
